builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoopPrune: Recurrent Pruning for Looped Diffusion Transformers
summary: LoopPrune replaces deploying a full dense looped diffusion Transformer with a structured-pruned version whose shared blocks are selected via recurrent importance estimation and recovered by distillation-style loop-position matching against a frozen dense teacher. The cost is an offline pruning-plus-recovery training phase requiring the teacher and data access, added pipeline complexity, and a residual quality gap (about 6.9% average accuracy loss at 30% pruning in the reported setting). It can fail if the target model is not a looped/shared-block architecture, if the recovery training is under-resourced, or if position-specific errors compound across recurrent iterations and degrade outputs beyond the reported benchmarks.
rationale: Structured pruning with a documented recovery procedure directly reduces GPU memory and latency on a single 24 GB card, but the gains are demonstrated on looped diffusion models and require retraining-based recovery, so it must be validated on the reader's specific model before adoption.
technique: Recurrent structured pruning of looped diffusion Transformers

claims.statement: LoopPrune replaces deploying a full dense looped diffusion Transformer with a structured-pruned version whose shared blocks are selected via recurrent importance estimation and recovered by distillation-style loop-position matching against a frozen dense teacher. The cost is an offline pruning-plus-recovery training phase requiring the teacher and data access, added pipeline complexity, and a residual quality gap (about 6.9% average accuracy loss at 30% pruning in the reported setting). It can fail if the target model is not a looped/shared-block architecture, if the recovery training is under-resourced, or if position-specific errors compound across recurrent iterations and degrade outputs beyond the reported benchmarks.

At 30% structured pruning, SDXSv3 reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 34.36-44.64% and accelerates denoising 1.46-1.74x over dense models across PyTorch, vLLM-Omni, and SGLang Diffusion; Looped-DiT B/16 retains 93.14% of dense average accuracy.
